terms.grammar: gerundive in the dative of purpose
terms.comment: A description of ours, built like decemvirī lēgibus scrībundīs: harēnātum is lime-and-sand mortar (Cato, Vitruvius). No reference work has a word for a cement mixer; Traupman’s māchina mixtōria is a kitchen mixer.
Traupman’s word for a kitchen mixer, which serves on a site when the context makes it clear; see “mixer”.

phrases.english: See how the cement mixer turns the mortar over?

phrases.latin: Māchina harēnātō miscendō strepit; nōlī accēdere.
phrases.english: The cement mixer is loud; don’t go near it.

sources: Lewis & Short: machina · Lewis & Short: harenatus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 346.
